candidate.answerReason: Adding the equations gives x+y+z=6, which determines x=1, y=2, and z=3. These values satisfy all three equations.

methods.label: Add all three equations
methods.explanation: Adding the three equations gives \(2(x+y+z)=12\), so \(x+y+z=6\). Subtracting each equation in turn gives \(z=6-3=3\), \(x=6-5=1\), and \(y=6-4=2\).
methods.levelReason: Adding and subtracting linear equations uses Grade 7 elimination.

methods.label: Express y and z using x
methods.explanation:
Expressing both \(y\) and \(z\) in terms of \(x\) reduces the remaining equation to one unknown. From \(x+y=3\) and \(x+z=4\), we have \(y=3-x\) and \(z=4-x\). Substituting into \(y+z=5\) gives
\[
(3-x)+(4-x)=5,
\]
so \(7-2x=5\) and \(x=1\). Then \(y=3-1=2\) and \(z=4-1=3\). The requested values are \(1,2,3\).
methods.levelReason: This alternative uses Grade 7 substitution and a simple linear equation, at the same prerequisite level as the main method.
